annotation.authors_or_issuer: Pino, M.; Rigaud, A.S.; Dacunha, S.; Vallée, R.; Ogawa, T.; Choi, M.; et al.
key_provisions_or_claims: Training health professionals is needed to handle consent, impaired judgment and attachment risks with cognitively impaired older adults.
Robot expressiveness and subject-like introduction increase perceived trustworthiness.
Older adults with cognitive decline struggle to understand robot speech, so accessible communication features are needed.
Public perceptions of care robots in South Korea vary, calling for public communication and discussion.
Participatory design with older adults is essential for ethical integration of social robots.
annotation.summary_en: Symposium proposal and abstracts from the International Society for Gerontechnology on ethical issues of socially assistive robots in geriatric care, covering France, Japan and South Korea. Topics: consent, attachment, trust, comprehension of robot speech, public perceptions and participatory design, with a training module for professionals.
annotation.title_clean: Ethical dimensions in human-robot interactions in the field of gerontechnology
annotation.title_en: Ethical dimensions in human-robot interactions in the field of gerontechnology
